source_name: 2bi d.o.o. — Digitalni Kiosk product/company site
why_relevant: 2bi operates 'Digitalni Kiosk', described as the first digital wallet in Montenegro and now positioned as a licensed digital payment institution (AIS/PISP); cited as ~60k+ users. Its site announces new billers, parking payment zones, top-ups and bank partnerships (CKB, Parking servis Podgorica) — a direct read on non-bank merchant/biller rail expansion.

source_name: Apple App Store — Digitalni Kiosk listing (ME storefront)
why_relevant: App-store 'What's New' release notes are the fastest, most granular disclosure channel for wallet feature changes (new billers, QR schemes, card tokenisation, instant-payment support) — often weeks ahead of any press release.

source_name: Google Play — Digitalni Kiosk listing
why_relevant: Android is the dominant platform in Montenegro; Play listing gives install-count bands, update cadence and 'What's new' notes — a proxy for adoption and feature velocity of the leading local wallet.

source_name: Digitalni Kiosk official Facebook page (@mobilnoplacanje)
why_relevant: Montenegrin fintechs announce campaigns, new billers and merchant partnerships on Facebook before (or instead of) the website. Handle name 'mobilnoplacanje' is itself a useful local-term marker.

source_name: Logate — Digital Banking Universe (Montenegrin banking/payments software vendor)
why_relevant: Podgorica-based vendor selling digital-banking and payment platform components to financial institutions. Vendor press releases and case studies reveal which Montenegrin/regional banks are buying which rails — merchant-side and channel disruption visible before bank disclosures.

source_name: Fleka — product studio building on PSD2 APIs (ICT Cortex Fintech Committee chair)
why_relevant: Fleka's executive director chairs the ICT Cortex Fintech Committee; the firm builds products on top of PSD2 APIs and bank cores. Its blog/portfolio is an early indicator of which open-banking use cases are actually being commissioned in Montenegro.

source_name: eFiskal — Montenegrin e-fiscalisation / POS software vendor
why_relevant: Merchant-side POS/fiscalisation software for retail and hospitality. Product notes reveal how fiscal QR, mobile POS and payment integrations are bundled to Montenegrin merchants — the layer where card acceptance is won or lost.

source_name: Sekas — fiscal cash registers and POS systems, Montenegro
why_relevant: Local POS/ECR integrator (products Aria for hospitality, Allegra for retail/wholesale). Its solution pages are a practical inventory of what Montenegrin merchants actually run at the till and which payment integrations are offered.

source_name: Crnogorski Telekom — media centre / e-fiscalisation and AdeoPOS merchant offer
why_relevant: A telco acting as a non-bank merchant-services challenger: bundles invoicing/POS apps (AdeoPOS, Pantheon) with connectivity for SME merchants. Its press centre is a reliable, dated channel for merchant-side product launches.

source_name: Pošta Crne Gore — PostFiskal e-fiscalisation service for merchants
why_relevant: State postal operator competing as a non-bank merchant-services provider (fiscalisation platform plus payment/cash services). Useful for tracking how non-bank incumbents package merchant offers against banks.

source_name: Digitalizuj.Me — Montenegrin digital community news portal
why_relevant: Long-running local tech/startup outlet that covers app launches, cluster news and payment apps in Montenegrin. Frequently the only public write-up of a small local fintech launch, and a rich source of new actor names to snowball.

source_name: Naučno-tehnološki park Crne Gore (NTP) — news and Startup Index Crne Gore
why_relevant: Publishes the Startup Index Crne Gore 2026 (65 startups profiled, with Game Changer Montenegro, Ministry of Education/Science/Innovation and the Investment Agency) and CoffINO event write-ups. The index is a ready-made, dated roster of local startups — including fintech — with funding-source breakdowns.

source_name: Tehnopolis Nikšić — innovation-entrepreneurship centre (BitProblem, BitID, BoostMeUp, Protobit programmes)
why_relevant: Accelerator/incubator whose cohort and demo-day announcements are the earliest public trace of pre-product Montenegrin fintech teams — typically 12-24 months before any regulator or press mention.

source_name: Tracxn — FinTech startups in Montenegro (company database)
why_relevant: Aggregator listing ~102 Montenegro-registered fintech entities with funding status (10 funded, 1 Series A+) — including forex/crypto entities (AMarkets, GoDefi, Impact, Prosecure, GANNMarkets). Useful for actor discovery, but note many are foreign-founded entities domiciled in ME rather than domestic payment challengers.

source_name: Digitalna Imovina (BIRN Montenegro) — digital economy/assets investigative platform
why_relevant: BIRN-run platform covering Montenegro's digital-asset and digitalisation policy, with named-expert interviews (e.g. on the lack of digitalisation incentives). Reveals friction and policy gaps that shape whether wallet/QR challengers can scale.

source_name: CIN-CG (Centar za istraživačko novinarstvo Crne Gore) — crypto/digital money investigations
why_relevant: Investigative reporting on unregulated crypto/e-money activity in Montenegro. Surfaces grey-zone non-bank actors and MiCA-preparation dynamics that never appear in company press releases.

source_name: Kriptobroker.me — self-described first crypto brokerage in Montenegro
why_relevant: Non-bank crypto-side actor announcing consumer-facing exchange and (claimed) point-of-sale crypto acceptance. Weak signal for alternative merchant acceptance rails ahead of MiCA-aligned Montenegrin legislation.

source_name: ICT Cortex / Montenegrin fintech company pages on LinkedIn
why_relevant: Small Montenegrin fintechs and software vendors (Logate, Fleka, Amplitudo, INFINTECH, Coinis) announce launches, hires and partnerships on LinkedIn far more often than on their own sites. Also the fastest way to detect new entities and rebrands.

source_name: CEJN — Crnogorski elektronski sistem javnih nabavki (Portal javne nabavke), Tenders section
why_relevant: Mandatory national e-procurement system for all Montenegrin budget entities; every tender notice, tendering documentation, award decision and concluded contract for banking, payment, card, ATM and core-banking services must pass through it. Contract award records name vendor, value and dates that no vendor press release discloses.

source_name: Direktorat za politiku javnih nabavki, Ministarstvo finansija Crne Gore (former Uprava za javne nabavke / UJN)
why_relevant: Policy and methodology owner for Montenegrin public procurement: publishes the Law, bylaws (pravilnici), standard notice forms (Obrazac 18 etc.), annual reports on the procurement system, registration instructions for CEJN, and an 'EU tenderi' category. Best single pointer for understanding notice structure, field semantics and where each document type is published.

source_name: Komisija za zaštitu prava u postupcima javnih nabavki — Rješenja (procurement review body decisions)
why_relevant: Appeal decisions in procurement disputes. These name the contracting authority, the complaining and winning bidders, the technical specification at issue and the price — often disclosing competitive detail (who bid, on what terms) that never appears in the award notice alone. High signal for contested banking/POS/ATM tenders.

source_name: TED — Tenders Electronic Daily (EU Official Journal S series)
source_subtype: supranational tender/award gazette with open data
why_relevant: Publishes above-threshold and EU-funded notices; relevant for Montenegro via EU Delegation / IPA-funded contracts and any ME entity publishing to TED. Structured CPV-coded data (66xxx financial services, 30xxx card/terminal hardware, 72xxx IT services) makes it the most machine-friendly award source in the cell. Bulk/open datasets available.

source_name: ECEPP — EBRD Client eProcurement Portal (procurement, shortlisting and contract award notices)
why_relevant: Since EBRD moved client procurement off ebrd.com, ECEPP is the sole publication point for procurement, prequalification, shortlisting and contract award notices under EBRD loans/grants — including Montenegrin financial-sector and PIU-support assignments. A Montenegro 'PIU Support' notice was seen in results, confirming ME coverage.

source_name: EBRD project summary documents & news — Montenegro financial institutions portfolio
why_relevant: EBRD PSDs and press releases name the Montenegrin counterparty bank, facility size and product type (e.g. NLB Banka AD Podgorica EUR 18m package, CKB portfolio risk-sharing, Alter Modus MSME lines). These reveal which banks are recapitalising/expanding and therefore likely to buy channel and payment technology — leading indicators ahead of any tender.

source_name: World Bank — Montenegro Financial Infrastructure Modernization / SEPA alignment (TIPS Clone) project page and documents
why_relevant: The single most consequential ME payments project in the cell: an EUR 8m World Bank loan to adopt the Banca d'Italia TIPS clone and align with SEPA. Project appraisal documents and the associated procurement plan name components, implementing agency (Central Bank / Ministry of Finance) and planned contract packages for instant-payment infrastructure — i.e. a forward pipeline of payment-technology procurement.

source_name: World Bank Finances One — procurement notices and contract awards (country: Montenegro)
why_relevant: Structured, downloadable dataset of World Bank procurement notices and major contract awards by country and sector — gives vendor name, amount, signing date and procurement method for Bank-financed ME contracts, including any under the payments/SEPA and fiscal-stability operations.

source_name: Centralna banka Crne Gore — Tenderi i oglasi
why_relevant: The central bank is both a regulator and a buyer: it procures RTGS/payment-system components, cash-handling and coin/banknote services, IT and facilities. Its own tender page mirrors what it publishes on CEJN and is the natural place for SEPA/TIPS-related implementation tenders to surface first.

source_name: Pošta Crne Gore — Javne nabavke
why_relevant: State-owned post operates money transfer, bill payment and counter/cash services and is a heavy buyer of counter terminals, cash handling and payment software. Its procurement page is a targeted, low-noise feed of exactly the payment-adjacent contracts this cell exists to catch.
